newsitem.title: TURKEY: Former Ciller economic chief resigns in Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Former Ciller economic chief resigns in Turkey.

text.p: A former Turkish economic chief resigned from the conservative True Path Party (DYP) on Friday, deserting his mentor Tansu Ciller who left office last month after four years in top government jobs.
"I have seen that DYP's mission has become more difficult in recent months," Ufuk Soylemez, the former state minister in charge of the economy, said in a resignation letter.

Former banker Soylemez was the head of privatisation in a 1993-95 government headed by Ciller and became state minister in a True Path coalition with Islamists that collapsed under pressure from the secularist army in late June.

Dozens of deputies have quit Ciller's pro-Western party since the influential military began criticising her ruling partnership with former prime minister Necmettin Erbakan's Islam-based Welfare Party in February.
Ciller, a U.S.-trained economist, became Turkey's first woman prime minister in 1993. She was the foreign minister and deputy premier in Erbakan's year-old government.
But in recent weeks Ciller has come under renewed corruption charges dating from her time in office.
New Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz has welcomed many of the ex-Ciller deputies into his anti-Islamist coalition government.
